ClassificationMethod.description:
The classification methods ``POST /v1/classifications`` serves.

``rules`` remains the bounded synchronous path. ``llm`` is accepted only
through the durable job surface added at contract 0.14 (#1605), because a
pass can take minutes or hours. The detached worker still invokes the
existing classify tool, including ModelRouter's intimate-never-cloud gate.

Attributes:
    RULES: Keyword classification. No model, no key, no consent, no egress.
    LLM: Model-backed classification, returned as a durable job handle.
ClassificationMethod.title: ClassificationMethod

FolderWriterlessReason.description:
Why a scaffolded folder has no writer, so an empty one says why.

Attributes:
    CONTAINER: A grouping folder; notes are filed into its subfolders.
    OWNER_CURATED: Material the owner places by hand; no stage writes it.
    INDEXED_AT_PARENT: The stage covering this topic files one index in
        the parent folder instead.
    TEMPLATE_EXAMPLE: A scaffold example of a layout, never filled.
FolderWriterlessReason.title: FolderWriterlessReason

JobFailureCode.description:
Why a ``failed`` pipeline job failed, when the caller can act on it (#1877).

Closed and deliberately small: a code is published only for a failure the
*caller* can remedy — including by resubmitting the same request — never
for an operator-side fault, whose detail stays in the server log. Any other
failure is ``failure_code: null``. Each member is served only to a caller
declaring at least the minor it was published at, named below; an earlier
caller is served ``null`` for the same failure.

Attributes:
    REQUEST_KEY_REJECTED: The writer's request-scoped provider key
        (ADR-0015) was refused by its vendor with ``401``/``403``. The
        pass stopped at the first refusal, without retrying, and nothing
        it had not yet started was sent. Retrying with the same key will
        fail the same way; the writer must replace the key. Since
        contract 0.26.
    BUSY: Another writer held the vault content-mutation lock past its
        bounded wait (#2075). The pass takes that lock before touching any
        fragment, so a timeout taking it means nothing was written; and
        both passes are idempotent and resumable, so a resubmit converges
        either way. The condition is transient — the same one the
        synchronous routes answer ``503 temporarily_unavailable`` — so
        resubmit the same request, with backoff. Since contract 0.29.
JobFailureCode.title: JobFailureCode

JobState.description: The closed lifecycle vocabulary for a durable pipeline job.
JobState.title: JobState

LinkMethod.description:
The linker stages ``POST /v1/links`` serves.

All four :data:`creek.surface_modes.LINK_METHODS` values are expressible.
``embeddings`` uses the durable job surface because it is the O(n²)
pairwise-similarity stage; the other three retain their synchronous
byte-identical ``200`` responses.

**Excluding it does not make every served member cheap, and the schema
should not be read as promising that.** ``eddies`` and ``threads`` both
need vectors, so both fill the embeddings parquet on a cold cache — a
local sentence-transformer pass over every uncached fragment, which is
minutes of work on a large vault and can outrun the request deadline.
They are served anyway because the parquet is a *cache*: the work a
timed-out first call performs still lands, so a retry converges instead of
starting over. Nothing about that reaches a network provider; the model is
local (ADR-0004). Budget for the first call on a cold vault, and prefer
``temporal`` when you only need the corpus navigable.

Attributes:
    TEMPORAL: Same-window adjacency links. The one genuinely cheap stage —
        no vectors, no model — and the one that makes a freshly-seeded
        corpus navigable at all.
    EDDIES: Topic clusters, materialised under ``03-Eddies/``. Embeds on a
        cold cache.
    THREADS: Narrative currents, materialised under ``02-Threads/``. Embeds
        on a cold cache, and reads the APTITUDE labels a classification
        pass writes, so run classification first.
    EMBEDDINGS: Pairwise similarity links, returned as a durable job handle.
LinkMethod.title: LinkMethod

PipelineDocumentStatus.description:
One document this caller uploaded, and the stages it has been through.

Attributes:
    external_id: The caller's own idempotency key for the upload.
    filename: The filename the caller sent.
    fragment_path: The first fragment's vault-relative path. Nullable in
        the schema, but a document with an unresolvable fragment is
        withheld (its tier cannot be proven), so a listed one names it.
    fragment_count: How many fragments the upload produced.
    stages: ``ingested`` first, then each later stage that has covered the
        document, in pipeline order. A stage not yet run is absent.

external_id.title: External Id

fragment_path.description: The first fragment's vault-relative path; null when gone.

PipelineDocumentStatus.title: PipelineDocumentStatus

PipelineFolderStatus.description:
One scaffolded ontology folder: how much it holds, and what fills it.

Attributes:
    path: The vault-relative folder path.
    count: Notes attributed to this folder, every tier counted. A note
        counts toward the deepest scaffolded folder holding it, so a nested
        scaffolded folder is never counted twice.
    last_written_at: The newest such note's modification time, or ``None``
        when the folder holds none.
    writer: The subsystem that writes here, or ``None``.
    writer_reason: Why nothing writes here, or ``None`` when ``writer``
        is set. Exactly one of the two is non-null.

last_written_at.description: Newest note's modification time, UTC; null when empty.
last_written_at.title: Last Written At

writer.title: Writer

writer_reason.description: Why nothing writes here; null when writer is set.

PipelineJobSummary.description:
One of this caller's durable pipeline jobs, counts-free.

Attributes:
    job_id: The job's opaque id, as ``GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}`` takes it.
    kind: ``classification`` or ``link``.
    method: The method the job runs.
    state: Its lifecycle state, read without side effects: a queued or
        running job no live worker owns reads ``failed``, as
        ``GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}`` would record it.
    failure_code: Why a failed job failed, when the caller can remedy it.
    updated_at: When the job record last changed.

A stage a document can have been through, in pipeline order.

Attributes:
    INGESTED: The upload landed as one or more fragments.
    CLASSIFIED: A classify pass ran over the vault after it landed.
    PRAXIS_SCANNED: The praxis passes ran (inside classify): the keyword

How the pass behind one stage row ended.

Attributes:
    OK: Completed with nothing left over.
    PARTIAL: Completed, but left work a retry of the same stage picks up.
    FAILED: Refused before it did its work; no later pass has succeeded.

One stage a document has been through.

Attributes:

WireTierCeiling.description:
The only two tier ceilings expressible on ``/v1``.

``/v1`` is remote by construction, and
:func:`creek_mcp.policy.admitted_ceiling` refuses any remote call declaring
a ceiling outside :data:`creek_mcp.policy.REMOTE_ADMITTED_CEILINGS` *before
dispatch*. Since #1073 that decision is transport-neutral, so every adapter
is meant to reach it the same way; the MCP surface does so today through
:meth:`creek_mcp.server._BoundedFastMCP.call_tool`, and #1074 mounts the
``/v1`` handlers that will. This enum mirrors that frozenset, so
``intimate`` and ``all`` are not merely refused at runtime — they cannot be
constructed at all, which is the half of the guarantee that does not depend
on a handler remembering to ask.

The same two values double as the wire's *tier* vocabulary (see
:class:`JournalUpsertRequest`, :class:`JournalUpsertResponse` and
:class:`ReflectionResponse`). The two vocabularies coincide by
construction: the set of tiers a remote caller may name is exactly the set
of ceilings a remote caller may declare, because a tier above the remote
cap is one no remote request can reach in either direction.

Attributes:
    OPEN: Openly publishable content only (ontology §13.2).
    PERSONAL: Adds personal — and, per #961, ``unclassified`` — content.
WireTierCeiling.title: WireTierCeiling

description:
What the pipeline has done: per folder, per document, per job.

Read-only: computing it triggers no stage and writes nothing.

Attributes:
    status: Always ``"ok"``.
    tier_ceiling: The caller's declared ceiling.
    folders: Every scaffolded ontology folder, in path order, including
        empty and writerless ones.
    documents: This caller's most recently landed uploads, newest first,
        at most the requested ``limit``. A document with any fragment above
        the ceiling is withheld, never named.
    documents_withheld: How many of the requested documents were withheld
        for the ceiling. Counted so a short page is not read as complete.
    jobs: This caller's most recent durable pipeline jobs, newest first.
